text:
maria: FYI CI flagged a perf regression on PR #9372 — microbench thresholds exceeded

ci-bot: [ci.redwood.internal] perf/unit tests failed for PR #9372: https://ci.redwood.internal/ci/9372 
- test: microbench/step_latency (baseline -> current: +22.4%)
- test: microbench/kv_cache_hit_rate (baseline -> current: -8.7%)
thresholds: 10%

sam: Ugh. Any idea which commit in the PR triggered it?

maria: The PR touches kernel selector and batching heuristics. Attaching perf diff from CI artifact: /artifacts/9372/perf-diff.txt

kevin: I'm grabbing the PR locally. Running `./scripts/run_microbench --name step_latency --runs 50` now.

jess: perf-bot posted the unit-test failure output too, looks like the CI run used the new `prefer_generic_matmul` path for int8 models. Could be a kernel selection regression.

perf-bot: perf-unit:microbench:step_latency: baseline=12.8ms current=15.7ms diff=+22.7% -> FAIL
perf-unit:microbench:kv_cache_hit_rate: baseline=0.92 current=0.84 diff=-8.7% -> FAIL

kevin: Local repro confirmed on my machine with commit 0fa9b7a (from feature/kernel-route). Running bisect now.

sam: If it's kernel selection, maybe a recent heuristic change prefers a generic matmul on small batch sizes. That would hit a lot of short requests and kill latency. Also check KV cache semantics — if prefix caching is skipped that can blow per-token cost.

kevin: bisect log:
```
git bisect start
good 8c3d4a2
bad 0fa9b7a
# bisecting: 5 revisions left to test
# commit 0fa9b7a: prefer_generic_matmul for int8
# result: bad (step_latency +20%)
```

kevin: Found the regress change. The kernel selector now prefers `matmul_generic_int8` for layers with <128 heads due to a cost-model bug (compute cost normalized incorrectly by seqlen). That kernel has worse fuse/kcache behavior -> more mem copies -> worse KV hit ratio.

maria: Nice find. Can we patch the cost model quickly or should we revert? This is blocking rollout and CI gates.

jess: Revert is faster to unblock. Let's open a revert PR and also add a perf unit test that asserts we don't pick `matmul_generic_int8` for the affected shapes.

sam: I'll draft the revert: PR #9381 reverting 0fa9b7a and add the test. Also adding a CI microbench that runs on small batch sizes + short context.

maria: Sounds good. Sam, please include the bisect notes in the PR description and link the CI artifact.

sam: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-inference/pull/9381 — revert + perf test. Triggering CI.

ci-bot: CI started for PR #9381. Running perf/unit microbench suite.

perf-bot: perf-unit:microbench:step_latency: baseline=12.8ms current=12.6ms diff=-1.6% -> OK
perf-bot:perf-unit:microbench:kv_cache_hit_rate: baseline=0.92 current=0.91 diff=-1.1% -> OK

maria: CI green on revert. Merging revert to main now. :white_check_mark:

kevin: After merge, I re-ran the full nightly microbench suite — numbers back to baseline. Verified KV cache hit pattern restored (no extra memcopies in trace).

jess: Follow-ups: (1) patch cost-model math to fix normalization bug, (2) add a synthetic perf regression test for kernel selection, (3) improve CI artifacts to include kernel selection decision in perf logs so future failures show which kernel was chosen. I'll make tickets.

maria: Thanks everyone. Good triage. Leaving notes in the rollback channel and the PRs.

sam: Add one more: increase sensitivity on the microbench that covers small-batch int8 models, but keep flaky tolerance — we almost had false positives on noisy runs.

kevin: I'll attach the flamegraph and perf traces to the follow-up ticket so the kernel author can debug.

maria: Closing the loop: revert merged, rollout unblocked, new perf tests + tickets opened: TKT-2147 (cost-model fix), TKT-2148 (kernel-selection perf test), TKT-2149 (CI artifact improvements).

jess: :thumbsup:
